Dated this the 10th day of April , 2025 The 3rd Respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No.573/ 2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manjeri, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the wife and minor children of the deceased Palaniswami, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.11.2011.

According to them, on 29.11.2011, at about 4.00 p.m., while the deceased was riding a motorcycle through the Palakkad-Calicut NH road, a bus bearing Reg.No. KL-10-S-6686 driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries, on 09.12.2011, while under treatment.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:33020 offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.9,55,00/-, limited to Rs.8,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs. 14,70,168/- (rounded to 14,70,500/-)
and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:

sentences.text: Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.A.R George, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/3rd respondent,
and Smt.M. Manju the learned Counsel for the claimants.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that, the Tribunal has added 30% of the income towards future prospects instead of 25% and deducted only 1/4 th of the income instead of 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses.

It was also argued that towards funeral expenses the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 25,000/-, towards loss of love and affection Rs. 3,00,000/- was awarded, in addition to Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium.

11. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that, the notional income of the deceased fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and that the compensation awarded on the head pain and suffering is also on the lower side.
12. According to the petitioners, the deceased was working as a coolie, earning Rs. 10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5,500/-.The
learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

13. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a 2025:KER:33020 coolie, during the year 2011 will come to Rs.8000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the petitioners could not prove the income of the deceased, as claimed in the OP, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8,000/-.
14.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 45 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income alone is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 14, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was married who left behind 3 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.11,20,000/-.
15.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs. 1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs. 3,00,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards 2025:KER:33020 funeral expenses,
and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, towards loss of The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Devaki on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31289991/
3 estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.

16.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.

17. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
Though the accident was on 29.11.2011 the deceased died only on 09.12.2011, after 11 days.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and 2025:KER:33020 reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.13,55,768/-
